name: Roland D-110
source: Roland D-110 Owner's Manual (MIDI Implementation 'Date: Mar. 1 1988, Version 1.00', printed pp.114-120: address map, *5-1..*5-8, RQ1/DT1 examples; PCM Sounds Table pp.103-104 and 57; tone parameter chapter pp.53-66; timbre/part pp.43-44, 69; system setup pp.80-82; structure + reverb chart p.133), https://static.roland.com/assets/media/pdf/D-110_OM.pdf (scanned; read from 300 dpi renders). Cross-checked against Edisyn edisyn/synth/rolandd110/RolandD110Tone.java + RolandD110Multi.java (github.com/eclab/edisyn, librarianTested): same addresses, 246-byte tone, 58-byte partial order, PCM bank bit packing, partial-mute bit order, test-patch procedure.

roland.checksum: Sum the 3 address bytes + data bytes (DT1) or the 3 address + 3 size bytes (RQ1); checksum = (128 - (sum % 128)) % 128. Manual examples verified: F0 41 10 16 11 04 01 76 00 01 76 0E F7 (RQ1 part 2 tone temp, 246 bytes); F0 41 10 16 12 40 01 04 4B 00 70 F7 (write part 3 timbre temp into I-B24).

messageFormat.RQ1: F0 41 <dev> 16 11 <a1 a2 a3> <s1 s2 s3> <sum> F7 -- answered by DT1(s) only if the address is a PARAMETER BASE ADDRESS (the start of an area in the map) and size >= 1 (manual p.116)

roland.deviceId: dev = Exclusive Unit # - 1 (Unit # 17-32 -> 10h-1Fh; factory 17 -> 10h) for every 'Unit #' area (03, 04, 05, 06, 08, 10, 20, 40). The 02 00 00 tone temp is instead addressed by a part's basic channel: dev = that part's MIDI channel - 1 (00h-0Fh). This schema uses only Unit # areas.
roland.addressing: 3 address bytes of 7 bits (00-7F each, carry at 128). Param 'offset' is a LINEAR byte index in its block; address = block base + offset with 7-bit carry: partial 1 starts at linear 14 (04 00 0E), 2 at 72 (04 00 48), 3 at 130 (04 01 02), 4 at 188 (04 01 3C); partial p param at partial offset o = 14 + 58(p-1) + o. Sizes encode the same way: 246 = 00 01 76.

tone.desc: Tone Temporary Area, part 1 (04 00 00, 00 01 76 bytes): common 00-0D (14 bytes), partial 1 at 0E, 2 at 48, 3 at 01 02, 4 at 01 3C (58 = 3A bytes each). THE edit buffer. Part n at 04 00 00 + 246*(n-1): part 2 04 01 76, part 7 04 0B 44, part 8 04 0D 3A.

timbre1.desc: Timbre Temporary Area, part 1 (03 00 00, 16 bytes; part n at 03 00 10*(n-1), rhythm part 03 01 00). Tone group/number, key shift, fine, bend, assign, output assign, dummy, level, pan, key range, 4 dummies. Context only (notInPatch).

system.desc: System Area (10 00 00, 00 00 21): master tune, reverb mode/time/level, partial reserve x9 (04-0C), MIDI channel x9 (0D-15), dummy (16), current patch name (17-20). Context only (notInPatch).

reserve.rule: sum of the 9 values <= 32; send all 9 in one DT1 (manual: 'All Partial reserves must be sent as a package of 9 parts'; the D-110 applies them only after all arrive)

requests.editBuffer: ONE RQ1 for the whole part-1 tone: F0 41 10 16 11 04 00 00 00 01 76 05 F7 (246 bytes). Do NOT RQ1 the common/partial sub-blocks separately: 04 00 0E etc. are offsets, not parameter base addresses, and the D-110 only answers RQ1s that start on a base address. The reply may arrive as one or several DT1s; collect by address.
requests.timbreAll: F0 41 10 16 11 03 00 00 00 01 10 6C F7 (parts 1-8 + rhythm, 9 x 16 = 144 bytes; Edisyn's request)

tone.desc: Tone Memory i-01..i-64: tone n (0-63) at 08 (2n) 00 -- 08 00 00, 08 02 00 ... 08 7E 00. Same 246-byte layout as the tone temp area (Edisyn pads memory writes to 256 bytes with 10 zeros; 246 is enough).

timbre.desc: Timbre Memory I-A11..I-B88 (#1-128): timbre n at 05 00 00 + 8n (05 07 78 = #128). 8 bytes: tone group, tone number, key shift, fine tune, bender range, assign mode, output assign, dummy.

patch.desc: Patch Memory I-11..I-88 (#1-64): patch n at 06 nn 00, 00 01 00 bytes: name 00-09, reverb mode/time/level 0A-0C, partial reserve x9 0D-15, MIDI ch x9 16-1E, 8 x 12-byte part blocks at 1F/2B/37/43/4F/5B/67/73 (tone group, tone #, key shift, fine, bend, assign, output assign, dummy, level, pan, key lo, key hi), rhythm output level 7F.

writeRequest.desc: Write Request area 40 00 00 (manual *5-8) = the panel WRITE button over MIDI. DT1 2 bytes [number, 0 = internal / 1 = card]: tone of part p -> 40 00 (2(p-1)) [tone 0-63, dest]; timbre of part p -> 40 01 (2(p-1)) [timbre 0-127, dest]; current patch -> 40 02 00 [patch 0-63, dest]. The D-110 reports the result at 40 10 00: 0 = completed, 1 = card not ready, 2 = write protected, 3 = incorrect mode. Nothing in 40 xx xx can be read with RQ1.

otherAreas.toneTempByChannel: 02 00 00 = Tone Temporary Area of whichever synth part listens on the MIDI channel encoded in dev (dev = channel - 1). Same 246-byte layout. Not used here.
otherAreas.rhythmSetupTemp: 03 01 10: 85 keys (note 24-108) x 4 bytes [tone 0-127 (i01-i64 = 0-63, r01-r64 = 64-127), output level 0-100, pan 0-14, output assign 0-7]; key k at 03 01 10 + 4(k-24), last (108) at 03 03 60 (= 03 01 10 + 00 02 50); size 340 = 00 02 54. Only a temporary area -- there is no rhythm-setup memory in the map.
otherAreas.display: 20 00 00: 32 ASCII chars written to the LCD (00-1F); any byte at 20 01 00 resets the display. Write-only.

encodings.bits: param.bits = {shift, width}: the param is a bit field inside a shared byte. Read: (byte >> shift) & ((1 << width) - 1). Write: byte = (byte & ~(mask << shift)) | (v << shift), taking the other bits from the current values of the sibling params (same block + offset) -- never send just this param's bits.
encodings.d110pcm: 2 bytes at offset o, o+1: byte o bit 1 = PCM bank (0 = bank 1, 1 = bank 2), byte o bit 0 = synth waveform (belongs to the *Waveform param, preserve it), byte o+1 = wave # 0-127. value = ((b0 >> 1) & 1) * 128 + b1. Write: b0 = (waveformBit) | ((v >> 7) << 1), b1 = v & 127; send both bytes in one DT1 (Edisyn does).

roland.notes: A TONE never sounds by itself: only a patch part pointing at it plays. Part 1 of the current patch has its own tone temp copy (04 00 00); editing it is heard on part 1's MIDI channel (factory ch 2, NOT ch 1). Selecting a patch (PC on the control channel) or a timbre (PC on the part's channel) or DT1ing part 1's tone group/number reloads 04 00 00 from memory/ROM and throws away unsaved edits. Firmware: 1.13 good, 1.10 fine, 1.07 broken for SysEx (Edisyn), 1.06 reported to crash on real-time parameter DT1s. Leave >= 20 ms between DT1s (llamamusic 1.07 notes via Edisyn: 25 ms per param, 100 ms after a whole-tone send, 275 ms between batch downloads).

structuresNote: Structure 1&2 pairs partial 1 (upper) with 2 (lower); 3&4 pairs 3 (upper) with 4 (lower). S = synth partial (square/saw WG + TVF), P = PCM partial (sample; its TVF params are ignored). A ring structure with one partial muted outputs the other dry (manual p.55). Diagram: manual p.133 / Edisyn Structure1-13.png.
pcmWavesNote: value 0-255 of the *PcmWave params: 0-127 = bank 1 #001-128, 128-255 = bank 2 #001-128. Bank 1: 001-030 rhythm, 031-073 attack, 074-111 sustained (loop), 112-128 decay 'Shot' (noise/clicks possible in some TVA ENV settings). Bank 2: 001-030 = the rhythm sounds again (marked *, not affected by master tune), 031-094 Loop-1..64 (repeats of one sound), 095-128 Jam-1..34 (repeats of combined sounds).

programs.note: There is no bank select (CC0/32 are ignored). The editor's edit buffer is a TONE, so only kind 'tone' banks are programs in the usual sense; 'patch' and 'timbre' banks exist for backup/restore. See driverNotes for how each is selected, read and written.

backup.notInSysex: Control Channel, Memory Protect, Exclusive Unit #, Overflow Assign are panel-only (no address). Card patches/timbres/tones have no address; copy them to internal memory on the panel first.
backup.restore: DT1 the saved bytes back to the same addresses with Memory Protect OFF, >= 20 ms apart. Restore tone memory and timbre memory before patch memory (patches reference tones by group/number).

setup: Firmware: check the ROM version at power-up. 1.13 (and 1.10) work; 1.07 is known broken for SysEx and 1.06 has crashed on real-time parameter messages (Edisyn). If it misbehaves, turn off live knob sends and send whole tones only.
[SYSTEM] > Mem Protect = OFF. It comes back ON at every power-up (manual p.81), so repeat this each session before writing tones or patches.
[SYSTEM] > Overflow = OFF. Early ROMs fail SysEx dumps with Overflow on (Edisyn).
[SYSTEM] > Exclu Unit# = 17 (Device ID 10h, the editor default).
[SYSTEM] > Control Ch. = a channel no part uses (e.g. 1), or OFF. Program changes on that channel switch whole patches, which also reloads part 1's tone.
Pick the editor channel = part 1's MIDI channel: factory part 1 = ch 2 (parts 1-8 = ch 2-9, rhythm = ch 10).

Make part 1 able to play the tone ('Set up test patch'): part 1 reserve = 32 and the others 0 (F0 41 10 16 12 10 00 04 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 4C F7), optionally other parts' channels OFF (9 bytes at 10 00 0D), part 1 level 100 (F0 41 10 16 12 03 00 08 64 11 F7) and pan centre (F0 41 10 16 12 03 00 09 07 6D F7). Then send the tone to 04 00 00.

Cable both ways: interface out -> D-110 MIDI IN, D-110 MIDI OUT -> interface in (RQ1 replies need the return path). Play nothing while requesting: RQD handshake requests are rejected while the D-110 is sounding, and it is safest to assume the same for RQ1.
driverNotes: The current rolandDriver assumes the JV-1080. For the D-110 it must change: (1) ADDRESSES/SIZES ARE 3 BYTES: toInt stays generic, but toAddr must emit R.addressBytes bytes ([(n>>14)&127,(n>>7)&127,n&127]); the size field of RQ1 is R.sizeBytes = 3 bytes; incoming DT1 parsing must read 3 address bytes (A..A+3) and data from A+3. (2) ONE BLOCK, ONE RQ1: the edit buffer is the single 246-byte 'tone' block at 04 00 00 -- request it with one RQ1 (size 00 01 76) and collect however many DT1s answer (the existing multi-DT1 collector is fine). Never RQ1 an offset inside it. sendPatch = one 246-byte DT1 to 04 00 00, then wait ~100 ms. (3) CONTEXT BLOCKS: 'timbre1' and 'system' hold only notInPatch params; exclude them from sendPatch/requestPatch/writeProgram/sameProgram (they already are, via notInPatch), but do read them once after connect (RQ1 03 00 00 size 10 and 10 00 00 size 21) so the part/reverb controls show real values, and send them only via sendParam. (4) BIT FIELDS: params with 'bits' {shift,width} share a byte (partial mute at tone 0C for p1On..p4On; waveform bit 0 of each partial's byte 04). encode/decode must mask, and sendParam must rebuild the whole byte from the current values of every param at that block+offset before sending it. (5) ENCODING 'd110pcm' (the *PcmWave params, size 2 at partial offset 04): check p.encoding BEFORE the size-2 'nibble' path; value = bank*128 + wave; write [waveformBit | (bank << 1), wave & 127] as one 2-byte DT1, merging the sibling *Waveform bit. In blockBytes, apply 'bits'/'d110pcm' params as masks over the lastData bytes so neither clobbers the other (apply *Waveform after *PcmWave, or merge). (6) PACKAGES: reserve1..reserveR (package 'reserve') must go out as one 9-byte DT1 at 10 00 04 built from all nine current values, and the editor should refuse/clip a total > 32. (7) USER MEMORY: userPatchFirstByte does not apply. Tone slot n lives at 08 00 00 + 256*n (7-bit: 08 (2n) 00), same 246-byte layout, so requestProgram = RQ1 08 (2n) 00 size 00 01 76 (no need to disturb part 1), and writeProgram = one 246-byte DT1 to 08 (2n) 00 (Memory Protect must be OFF; the D-110 gives no acknowledgement for a direct memory DT1, so read it back and compare, as the editor already does). Generic form: addr(n) = toInt(userMemory[kind].base) + n*userMemory[kind].stride. Alternative write path: DT1 the edit buffer to 04 00 00, then DT1 40 00 00 [n, 0] (write request = panel WRITE of part 1's tone to i-(n+1)) and listen for the DT1 result at 40 10 00 (0 ok, 1 card not ready, 2 write protected, 3 incorrect mode). After storing, DT1 03 00 00 [2, n] so part 1 points at the stored tone (that reload is harmless because memory now matches). (8) PROGRAM SELECT: there is no bank select. For kind 'tone' banks, programChange(bi, prog) = DT1 bank.select.address [group, prog] (2 bytes at 03 00 00) -- this loads that tone into part 1 (and discards unsaved edits); ROM a/b/r banks are read by selecting then requesting the edit buffer. Kind 'patch' banks select with PC (prog + offset) on the D-110 Control Channel (a separate channel setting, not the part channel); kind 'timbre' with PC on the part channel. Patch/timbre banks are backupOnly: backups RQ1 roland.userMemory[bank.memory] slot by slot and keep the raw DT1s; they are never loaded into the tone edit buffer. (9) DEVICE ID = Unit# - 1 (default 10h) for everything here; 02 00 00 (per-channel tone temp) would need dev = channel - 1 and is not used. (10) PACING: >= 25 ms between DT1s (gapMs), ~100 ms after a whole-tone DT1 or a program select before the next RQ1, 275 ms between slots in a batch backup; consider a user toggle to disable live per-knob sends for 1.06/1.07 firmware. (11) Front-panel edits are not echoed as DT1 while editing (the D-110 transmits only on ENTER / bulk dump), so decode() will rarely fire; keep it for dumps.
uncertain: P-ENV Velocity Sensitivity: the MIDI implementation prints 0-100 (bit mask '0aaa aaaa'), but the panel chapter (p.59) says 0-3 and Edisyn (hardware-tested) calls the table an error and uses 0-3. Modelled 0-3 -- the D-110 manual itself disagrees with itself; the panel chapter + Edisyn win.

P-ENV Sustain Level (partial offset 12): the MIDI table says '50 (always 0)' i.e. fixed; the panel chapter (p.60) lists Sustain Level -50..+50 and Edisyn credits a user with confirming it works on the D-110. Modelled as editable 0-100; if it is ignored on your unit, leave it at 50.

Partial mute bit order: the manual gives only '0-15 (0000-1111)' and shows the panel as 'PartialMute=1100' (partial 1 leftmost, 1 = sounds). Bit 0 = partial 1 comes from Edisyn (and the munt MT-32 emulator); Edisyn's init tone stores 01 = only partial 1 sounding, consistent with that. Verify by toggling p1On and listening.

Output Assign 0-7 is printed 'MIX, MIX, MULTI 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6' (8 values for 7 names); the panel shows only MIX and 1-6. Value 1's meaning is unknown (Edisyn labels 0/1/2 'Mix/Min/Mult', which does not match the manual). Options label value 1 as 'MIX (value 1)'; use 0 for MIX and 2-7 for multi 1-6 (not verified).
Patch Parameters (patch memory part block) TONE GROUP is printed 0-4 while the timbre areas print 0-3 (a, b, i/c, r). Probably a misprint; 0-3 is used.
Structures 8 and 9 are drawn as two unmixed partials; the pan chapter (p.69) shows they are split across the stereo field. Descriptions 'stereo pair' are from that table, not a dedicated statement.

Tone memory stride is 256 bytes (08 00 00, 08 02 00, ...) but a tone is 246 bytes. Edisyn writes 256 (246 + 10 zero bytes) to memory and reads 246; this schema reads and writes 246. If a 246-byte write to 08 (2n) 00 is not accepted, pad to 256 like Edisyn.

Write Request result: the manual says the D-110 'will inform back of the writing result' at 40 10 00 but does not show the message; it is assumed to be a DT1 F0 41 <dev> 16 12 40 10 00 <0-3> <sum> F7. Direct DT1s to memory (08/05/06) give no acknowledgement at all.

RQ1 while notes are sounding: the manual documents RJC (reject) for the RQD handshake while the unit 'is reproducing sound'; whether RQ1 is also ignored during notes is not stated. Request with no notes held.

The RQ1 rule 'address must be a parameter base address' (manual p.116) is why the tone is requested as one 246-byte block. Whether the D-110 also answers RQ1s at partial offsets (04 00 0E ...) is untested.
Master Tune 0-127 = 427.5-452.6 Hz (manual); the value for exactly 440 Hz is not given (probably 64).
Tone group r (rhythm) number 63 = OFF comes from the timbre chapter ('Preset Rhythm Tones are 01-63 and OFF'); the address map just says 0-63.
Reverb type names: MIDI table 'Room 1/2, Hall 1/2, Plate, Tap delay 1/2/3, OFF' vs chart p.133 'Small Room, Medium Room, Medium Hall, Large Hall, Plate, Delay 1-3'; both shown in the option labels.
Firmware notes (1.13 good, 1.10 fine, 1.07 broken, 1.06 crash on real-time sends) and 'Overflow must be OFF' are from Edisyn's docs/user reports, not from Roland.
Rhythm setup (03 01 10) has no memory address in the map; Edisyn says the D-110 resets it at power-up. It can be backed up but not stored on the unit.
